findings.highlight: your instructions are better as a magus
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師として遠坂の指示が優れてる
findings.governingReading: Shirou concedes that Rin’s directions are excellent from a magus’s standpoint.
findings.explanation: “Better” has no comparison target and “as a magus” attaches as though instructions themselves were acting in that capacity.

findings.highlight: I need someone to act as my brakes
findings.evidenceJa: ブレーキ役がいなくちゃ危ないって思ってた
findings.governingReading: Rin admits she tends to run ahead unchecked and has thought it dangerous not to have someone restrain her.
findings.explanation: The brake metaphor survives in Japanese-shaped English, but her explicit recognition of danger disappears.

findings.evidenceJa: ちょっと、拍子抜けした
findings.governingReading: Shirou is caught off guard and deflated because Rin accepts the objection he expected her to contest.
findings.explanation: Disappointment gives him negative dissatisfaction rather than an anticlimactic release of tension.

findings.highlight: I’ll help you as much as I can
findings.governingReading: Rin offers however much help is needed when she can do what Shirou cannot.
findings.explanation: “As much as I can” introduces a capacity ceiling absent from her deliberately expansive offer.

findings.highlight: Is it possible that she can’t cook and needs my help?
findings.evidenceJa: 実はこう見えて料理ベタだとか？
findings.governingReading: Shirou privately guesses that, appearances notwithstanding, Rin might actually be bad at cooking.
findings.explanation: The English omits the contrast with appearances, strengthens bad at cooking to unable to cook, and adds that she needs his help.

findings.evidenceJa: それは子供の我がままに似ていて
findings.governingReading: Her sulking demand resembles a child’s selfish insistence.
findings.explanation: The concrete behavioral comparison becomes a generic judgment that she looks childish.

findings.evidenceJa: きっと遠坂を勝たせる
findings.governingReading: Shirou promises that, as her partner, he will make sure Rin wins the Grail War.
findings.explanation: “Let you win” conventionally means deliberately yielding or throwing a contest, reversing active support into condescension.

findings.governingReading: Rin says the sessions at her house will continue for some time starting today.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the start but omits the stated continuing duration.

findings.highlight: you’ll be working overtime every day
findings.evidenceJa: 連日居残ってもらう事になる
findings.governingReading: Rin says she will have Shirou stay late after school day after day for training.
findings.explanation: “Working overtime” supplies employment language and obscures the school-day training arrangement.

findings.evidenceJa: 帰りはかなり遅くなる
findings.governingReading: Rin warns that he will get home considerably late.
findings.explanation: The degree of disruption to Shirou’s household plans is omitted.

findings.evidenceJa: 家で養生している桜には悪いが
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels guilty toward Sakura specifically because she is recuperating at his house.
findings.explanation: Her illness-related recuperation and presence in the house disappear, weakening the domestic obligation competing with training.
